beats.intro: Chapter three, lesson four. Denaturation and misfolding. [[egg]]Crack an egg into a hot pan. The clear, runny white turns solid and white in seconds. Nothing was added, and no atom was swapped. [[ask]]So what changed? The proteins in the egg white lost their shape. [[map]]Here is our strip of the four levels of structure, from lessons one to three. [[lit]]We built it up, step by step. Today we run it backwards, and watch it come apart.
beats.unfold: [[fold]]Here is a folded protein: helices, sheets and loops, packed into one compact shape. [[heat]]Now add heat. [[open]]The shape opens. The chain unfolds, and lies in an irregular tangle. [[def]]That is denaturation: the destruction of the secondary, tertiary and quaternary structures of a protein. The slide puts it in three words: denaturation means unfolding. [[one]]Notice that the chain is still one piece. Nothing was cut.
beats.strip: [[quat]]Let's run the strip backwards, from the top. The subunits of the quaternary structure come apart. [[tert]]Each subunit loses its folded globule, the tertiary structure. [[sec]]The helices and sheets of the secondary structure lose their hydrogen bonds, and open out. [[prim]]What is left is the primary structure: the same beads, in the same order, joined by the same peptide bonds. [[keep]]That is the key point. Denaturation breaks the weak bonds that held the fold. The strong peptide bonds stay. So this is not hydrolysis, and no amino acids are set free. Back in chapter two, these were the primary derivatives, such as coagulated albumin.
beats.causes: [[six]]The slide lists six causes of denaturation. [[heat]]First, high temperature: the frying pan. [[press]]Second, high pressure. [[shake]]Third, vigorous shaking, like whisking egg white until it stands in peaks. [[acid]]Fourth, strong acids and alkalis. Acid is what curdles milk. [[uv]]Fifth, ultraviolet light and other irradiation. [[xray]]And sixth, X-rays. [[group]]To remember them: heat and pressure, shaking, chemicals, and radiation.
beats.effects: [[five]]Denaturation has five effects. [[enz]]One, enzymes lose their catalytic activity, because the active site needs the folded shape. [[hor]]Two, hormones lose their biological function, for the same reason. [[sol]]Three, solubility falls. The unfolded chains stick together and clump. [[vis]]Four, viscosity rises, so the liquid thickens. [[dig]]Five, digestibility rises. [[cook]]That is why we cook meat and eggs: once the chain is unfolded, digestive enzymes can reach its peptide bonds. [[egg2]]It is also the coagulated albumin of chapter two. Solubility and viscosity change in the typical case, not for every protein.
beats.misfold: [[mis]]Now a different problem: misfolding. [[good]]A healthy protein folds into a stable three dimensional shape. [[bad]]A misfolded protein cannot. [[agg]]Misfolded chains stick to each other, and form aggregates: large, insoluble clumps. [[lose]]They lose their structure, and they lose their function. [[vs]]Compare the two. A denatured protein was folded, and something, like heat, unfolded it. A misfolded protein never reached a stable fold, and it clumps.
beats.alz: [[brain]]The best known example is Alzheimer's disease. [[amy]]Here a protein called amyloid beta misfolds. [[plaque]]Its aggregates are deposited as dense, fibrous plaques in the brain. [[tau]]A second protein, tau, also tangles inside nerve cells, but our slides focus on amyloid beta. [[neuro]]The nerve cells slowly degenerate. That is called neurodegeneration. [[sym]]The symptoms are memory loss, dementia, and a lack of recognition. [[hedge]]Amyloid beta plaques are the hallmark of the disease, and the leading explanation for its cause.
beats.case: [[card]]Now a case. A seventy-two-year-old man began, two years ago, forgetting recent events and conversations. [[now]]Recently he did not recognise his close relatives. His memory impairment is severe, and he has lost the ability to carry out everyday tasks. [[ask]]There are two questions. First: what is the diagnosis?
beats.q1: Quick check. What is the diagnosis?
beats.cause: [[link]]The diagnosis is Alzheimer's disease. The second question: mention the possible cause of this disease.
beats.q2: Quick check. What is the possible cause?
beats.solve: [[dx]]The diagnosis is Alzheimer's disease. [[cx]]The possible cause: misfolding of amyloid beta protein, which clumps into plaques in the brain.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[s1]]Denaturation is unfolding. Secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure are destroyed, and the primary structure stays. [[s2]]Heat, pressure, shaking, strong acids and alkalis, ultraviolet light and X-rays all do it. Enzymes and hormones lose their function, and the protein becomes less soluble, thicker, and easier to digest. [[s3]]Misfolding is different: the protein cannot reach a stable shape, and clumps into aggregates, as in Alzheimer's disease. [[chap]]And that closes chapter three. We met the bonds that hold a fold, then primary and secondary structure, then tertiary and quaternary, and now the way it all comes undone. [[end]]Shape is function. Now try the practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Six questions on denaturation and misfolding.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter three, lesson four, and the end of the chapter.
